newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka says over 250 killed in rebel attack.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka says over 250 killed in rebel attack.

text.p: Sri Lanka said on Wednesday that 58 special forces troops and 210 rebels were killed when Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) separatists attacked the military's northern forward defences.

The figures conflicted with the rebels' account of the pre-dawn attack which said the military casualty toll could be "Fifty-eight bodies of special forces troops were recovered in the clearing operation now going on," a Defence Ministry spokesman told Reuters.

The spokesman said some 1,000 rebels had taken part in the attack on the army's defences at Thandikulam and Nochchimoddai, north of the government-held frontline town of Vavuniya, 220 km (135 miles) north of Colombo.
He said 12 officers and 86 troops were wounded. More than 300 rebels were believed to have been wounded, he added.

The spokesman said the army destroyed three of its own artillery guns and some ammunition to prevent them from falling into the hands of the rebels, who are fighting for a homeland for minority Tamils in the Indian Ocean island's north and east.
He said the area where the attack took place was being cleared by the military and the rebels had withdrawn under fire.
"The area has stabilised completely. We have re-established our defences. Troops are still carrying out clearing operations in the area," the spokesman said.

The LTTE's clandestine Voice of Tigers radio, monitored in Vavuniya, said on Wednesday that military casualties could be It said late on Tuesday that the LTTE had killed more than 100 soldiers and that 50 rebels had also died during the attack in which a military ammunition dump and a key bridge near Nochchimoddai were destroyed.
Security forces last month launched Operation "Jaya Sikuru", or "Sure of Victory", on the rebels' northern Wanni stronghold from Thandikulam.
An aid worker in Vavuniya told Reuters that three civilians, including a seven-year-old girl, had been killed in the fighting. Some 28 were wounded and admitted to Vavuniya hospital, he added.
Military officials said the civilian death toll was expected to rise as many bodies had yet to be recovered from the area.
The Defence Ministry said the rebels had tried to dislodge the army's field headquarters and artillery positions at Thandikulam in an effort to disrupt the offensive.
It said the LTTE launched the attack in a bid to cut supplies to troops fighting further north.
Deputy Defence Minister Anuruddha Ratwatte told the state-owned Daily News that troops had expected the attack.
"We were prepared. When they (the rebels) can't attack the head they attack the tail. Even our tail is more powerful than their joint forces," Rattwatte was quoted as saying.
The rebels meanwhile warned of further attacks.
"The Sri Lanka army can expect many more military disasters like this in coming weeks," the LTTE's international spokesman, Anton Rajah, told Reuters from London.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
